# Part 1 · A payout table (12 points)
## (1a) The payout distribution, and its expectation two ways
```{r}
# Build payout for every flight
flights <- flights %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    payout = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(dep_delay) ~ 400,
      !is.na(dep_delay) & is.na(arr_delay) ~ 200,
      arr_delay > 180 ~ 200,
      arr_delay > 60 & arr_delay <= 180 ~ 50,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

# flights$payout # check column values


# Report the probability of each payout value
pCanceled <- mean(is.na(flights$dep_delay))
pCanceled

pDiverted <- mean(!is.na(flights$dep_delay) & is.na(flights$arr_delay))
pDiverted

p180Late <- sum(flights$arr_delay > 180, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(flights)
p180Late

pLate <- sum(60 < flights$arr_delay & flights$arr_delay <= 180, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(flights)
pLate


# Compute E[X] two ways - outputs must agree:

# 1) ... from the table

cashCanceled <- 400
cashDiverted <- 200
cash180Late <- 200
cashLate <- 50
cashOther <- 0 # cancels out

EPayout_theoretical <- (cashCanceled * pCanceled) + (cashDiverted * pDiverted) + (cash180Late * p180Late) + (cashLate * pLate)
EPayout_theoretical

# 2)  ... using mean() of the payout column

EPayout_actual <- mean(flights$payout)
EPayout_actual

isTRUE(all.equal(EPayout_theoretical, EPayout_actual))
EPayout_theoretical == EPayout_actual # Floating point error

```



## (1b) Where the expectation sits
The share of expected payouts from cancellations make up the tail of the distribution, and the expected overall payout sits just past the bulk of data (flights with $0 or $50 payouts) toward the skewed tail of the distribution.

```{r}

pCanceled # share of flights that are canceled

cancelContribtuion <- cashCanceled * pCanceled # payout per flight due to cancellations
cancelShareOfPayout <- cancelContribtuion / EPayout_actual 
cancelShareOfPayout 

```


## (1c) A fair fee, and a 900-flight day
A fair fee is the Expectation of the payout, $16.34, with the expected cost for 900 flights per day being $14,705.95. This Expectation is a linear model, meaning independence/dependence of flights is irrelevant. 

```{r}
E900 <- 900 * EPayout_actual
E900

```

# Part 2 · Sums are free, variances are not (16 points)
## (2a) Daily late counts by airport, and the total
```{r}

# Late arrival counts for each day and origin ----------------------------------
d_late_daily_origin <- d %>%
  dplyr::group_by(origin, day) %>%
  dplyr::filter(arr_delay > 15) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n = n())


# 1) Per-airport daily counts --------------------------------------------------
# Per airport daily  - JFK
jfk_daily_count <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "JFK"]
jfk_mean <- mean(jfk_daily_count) # average across days
jfk_var <- var(jfk_daily_count) # variance across days
sqrt(jfk_var)

# Per airport daily  - EWR
ewr_daily_count <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "EWR"]
ewr_mean <- mean(ewr_daily_count) # average across days
ewr_var <- var(ewr_daily_count) # variance across days
sqrt(ewr_var)

# Per airport daily  - LGA
lga_daily_count <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "LGA"]
lga_mean <- mean(lga_daily_count) # average across days
lga_var <- var(lga_daily_count) # variance across days
sqrt(lga_var)

# 2) Daily total across all three airports --------------------------------------
# Daily total of the three airports: JFK, EWR, LGA
d_late_daily_total <- d_late_daily_origin %>%
  dplyr::group_by(day) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(total_n = sum(n))

d_late_daily_total_mean <- mean(d_late_daily_total$total_n)
d_late_daily_total_var <- var(d_late_daily_total$total_n) # by how much the aggregated airports vary on a daily basis
sqrt(d_late_daily_total_var) # SD - how much the aggregated airports vary on a daily basis, # of flights


# 3) Does the mean of the total equal the sum of the three means? --------------
isTRUE(all.equal((jfk_mean + ewr_mean + lga_mean), d_late_daily_total_mean))


# 4) Variance of the total compared to the sum of the three variances ----------
d_late_daily_total_var / (jfk_var + ewr_var + lga_var)

# Ratio to describe linear relationship:
#   ratio ~ 1, covariance = 0
#   ratio > 1, covariance > 0, data vary positively
#   ratio < 1, covariance < 0, data vary negatively

```


## (2b) The covariance terms
```{r}

# Compute the 3 covariances between airports:
jfk_n <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "JFK"]

ewr_n <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "EWR"]

lga_n <- d_late_daily_origin$n[d_late_daily_origin$origin == "LGA"]

cov(jfk_n, ewr_n)
cov(jfk_n, lga_n)
cov(ewr_n, lga_n)

# Compute 3 correlations between airports:
cor(jfk_n, ewr_n)
cor(jfk_n, lga_n)
cor(ewr_n, lga_n)


```
